candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Apply HIPAA rules for disclosures to family or friends by confirming patient agreement or another permitted basis and limiting disclosure to information relevant to the person's involvement in care.

options.A: Refuse all communication because HIPAA prohibits telephone discussions with family members
options.B: Share only protected health information directly relevant to the daughter's involvement in the client's care, consistent with the client's permission and facility procedures
options.C: Disclose the client's complete medical record because the caller is a family member
options.D: Require a written HIPAA authorization for every routine disclosure to an involved family member even when the client has agreed

candidate.rationale: HHS explains that under 45 CFR 164.510(b), a provider may communicate with family, friends, or others involved in a patient's care when the patient agrees, does not object, or the provider can reasonably infer no objection. The disclosure must be limited to information directly relevant to that person's involvement. HIPAA does not categorically prohibit telephone communication or require written authorization for every such routine disclosure.
candidate.source_claim_supported: HIPAA permits relevant disclosures to family or others involved in care when the patient agrees or does not object; disclosures are limited to PHI directly relevant to that involvement. HIPAA itself does not require proof of identity from a caller merely claiming to be family or a friend, although organizations may adopt verification procedures.
candidate.source_document_title: HIPAA FAQ: Communications with Family, Friends, or Others Involved in a Patient's Care
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office for Civil Rights
candidate.stem: A competent client has told the healthcare team that an adult daughter is involved in the client's care and may receive relevant health information. The daughter later calls for an update. Which action is consistent with the HIPAA Privacy Rule?
